haiku-low.q1: Up to 10,000 rows (per reports.row_count): CSV streams straight back. Above that: a background job is queued, the record returned, and the user emailed a link.
haiku-low.q2: The unique partial index rejects the insert; the server returns the existing queued or running record and enqueues no new job.
haiku-low.q3: The signed link lasts up to 24 hours. Bucket lifecycle deletes objects after 7 days and incomplete uploads after 24 hours; no cleanup job.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts total. After the last, the record is set to failed, the user is emailed, and may start a new export.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Report rows are never read from the primary; the export record lives in the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table (primary database). The page loads GET /exports/latest on open and polls it while queued or running; poll interval undecided.
haiku-low.q7: 5,000-row keyset batches fill one in-memory buffer, uploaded as a multipart part near 8 MB; memory is one buffer plus one batch.
haiku-low.q8: Data is discarded and the next attempt restarts from the beginning with a fresh upload. Unfinished uploads are never visible and expire after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and column order are stored in the report_exports record; the job payload carries only the export id, and the handler loads the record.
haiku-low.q10: A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) for queued or running rows; the losing insert breaks it and the server returns the existing record.
haiku-low.q11: Upload completed and signed URL built before send_email; record set to done last. A rerun stops only if the record is already done.
haiku-low.q12: The download breaks and the user clicks again; nothing is stored and there is no export record.

sonnet.q1: The server reads reports.row_count (total unfiltered count, even if the view is filtered). 10,000 rows or fewer: small path, the response is the CSV itself, streamed. More than 10,000: large path, a background job builds it, stores it in object storage, and the user gets an emailed download link; the click immediately returns the export record.
sonnet.q2: The insert breaks the unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) for queued/running rows. The server returns the existing export record and enqueues nothing (no new job).
sonnet.q3: The signed URL lasts 24 hours (86,400 s, the maximum). The exports bucket's lifecycle rule deletes every object after 7 days; no cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts in total (waits of 60 s then 300 s). After the last fails, on_final_failure sets the record to failed and emails the user that the export failed; the page shows failed and the user may start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica. Report data is never read from the primary (only the export record lives in the primary).
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table (export record status: queued, running, done, failed) in the primary database. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load to get the most recent export's status, and polls that endpoint every few seconds while it is queued or running, so a returning user sees the current status.
sonnet.q7: It streams: multipart upload, pages the replica by keyset in 5,000-row batches into one in-memory buffer, uploads a part whenever the buffer reaches about 8 MB and empties it, then uploads the remainder as the final part and calls complete_multipart. Memory is one buffer plus one batch, never the whole report. (Whether 2 million rows finishes within the 1,800 s attempt timeout is unmeasured.)
sonnet.q8: If the handler raises, it aborts its multipart upload and re-raises. If the attempt times out or the worker dies, the abort doesn't run; the leftover upload is never completed, so nothing is downloadable, and the bucket discards it after 24 hours. Either way the next attempt starts from the beginning of the handler with a fresh upload (no resume), with the record staying running.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED for the job payload specifically. The document says the filters and column order are stored in the export record (report_exports table), taken from the page URL on the POST, and the job is enqueued with the export id; it does not explicitly say the handler reads them from the record.
sonnet.q10: The unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) for rows with status queued or running in report_exports; the second insert breaks it.
sonnet.q11: The file must be fully uploaded and complete_multipart must have succeeded, then a 24-hour signed URL is built; only then is the email sent, and afterwards the record is set to done. If the job runs again, the handler loads the record at the start of the attempt, sees done, and stops. (If it reruns before done was recorded, e.g. after an email error, it starts again from the beginning.)
sonnet.q12: The download breaks; no job, nothing stored, no export record. The user clicks again.
